title: Managing files in a Graphical User Interface (GUI) environment

lessons.title: Files, folders and drives
lessons.html:
Where the computer keeps your work

A GUI (graphical user interface) is the screen with pictures, windows and icons that you use with a mouse, like Windows. In a GUI your work is saved in files, and files are kept in folders.

Files

A file is one piece of work, for example a letter, a list of bales, a photo or a spreadsheet of wages. Every file has a name and a type. The type is shown by the letters after the dot, called the extension:

ExtensionType of file
.docxWord document
.xlsxExcel spreadsheet
.pdfPDF document
.jpgPhoto

Folders

A folder is like a box file in the office. It holds files and can hold other folders. Good folders make files easy to find, for example:

  • Wool Store
  • — Receiving 2026
  • — Dispatch 2026
  • — Staff

Drives

Drives are where files are stored: the computer's own hard drive (usually C:), a USB flash drive, or a network or cloud drive shared with others in the office.

File Explorer

In Windows you look at files and folders with File Explorer. Open it with the folder icon on the taskbar, or press the Windows key and E together. On the left you see drives and folders. Click a folder to see what is inside on the right.

lessons.title: Creating, naming and moving files
lessons.html:
Working with files and folders

Make a new folder

  1. Open File Explorer and go to the place for the new folder.
  2. Right-click an empty space, choose New, then Folder.
  3. Type the name and press Enter.

Good names

  • Use clear names: "Bale register March 2026" is better than "doc1".
  • Put dates as year-month-day, like 2026-03-15, so files sort in order.
  • Do not use these signs in names: \ / : * ? " < > |

Rename

Right-click the file, choose Rename, type the new name and press Enter. Do not change the extension.

Copy and move

  • Copy makes a second copy. Right-click, Copy, go to the new place, right-click, Paste. Or press Ctrl+C then Ctrl+V.
  • Move takes the file away from the old place. Right-click, Cut, then Paste in the new place. Or Ctrl+X then Ctrl+V. You can also drag a file to another folder.

Select many files

Hold Ctrl and click each file to choose several. Click the first file, hold Shift and click the last to choose all in between.

Search

If you cannot find a file, type part of the name in the search box in the top right of File Explorer.

Practise

Try this: make a folder called "Practice" on the desktop. Inside it, make a new file and name it with today's date. Copy it, rename the copy, and move it into a new folder inside "Practice". Then delete the copy and find it in the Recycle Bin.

lessons.title: Deleting, backing up and keeping files safe
lessons.html:
Look after the files

Delete and restore

  • Choose the file and press Delete, or right-click and choose Delete.
  • Deleted files go to the Recycle Bin. If you made a mistake, open the Recycle Bin, right-click the file and choose Restore.
  • When the Recycle Bin is emptied, the files are gone.
  • Files deleted from a USB drive or network drive may not go to the Recycle Bin. Be careful.
  • Never delete files that belong to someone else or that you do not understand. Ask first.

Back up

A backup is a second copy kept in a different place. If the computer breaks, is stolen or gets a virus, the backup saves the work. Follow your office's backup plan, for example copying to the network drive or cloud every day.

USB drives

  • Before pulling out a USB drive, click "Safely remove" or "Eject" so files are not damaged.
  • USB drives can carry viruses. Only use drives your office allows.
  • Do not keep the only copy of important files on a USB drive.

Keep files private

Some files, like wages and staff records, are private. Save them only in the folders your supervisor gives you, and lock the computer when you walk away.

Key points

  • Files hold your work; folders organise files; drives store them.
  • Use clear file names with dates as year-month-day.
  • Copy makes a second copy; cut and paste moves the file.
  • Deleted files go to the Recycle Bin until it is emptied.
  • Back up important files and eject USB drives safely.
